clue.text: Fare that would go down well with the ecology party

definitions.text: Fare that would go down well with the ecology party

parts.words: Fare that would go down well with the ecology party
parts.note: read as food that would please the Green Party, the environmentalist political party, it describes a seasonal leafy vegetable whose name contains that party's name

explanation.surface: A caterer plans a menu to please environmental campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greens are the British environmentalist party; the answer is young cabbage leaves eaten in early spring, so the dish literally carries the party's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Young cabbage leaves picked early in the year are a staple vegetable fare.

clue.text: Calmed down on retaining top journalistic post

parts.note: keeping on, continuing as before, is to be still going
ED is short for editor, the senior post on a newspaper

explanation.surface: A journalist is soothed on hearing they keep the editor's chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retaining' looks like a container signal but is part of the phrase for continuing; ED, the editor, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To quieten something is to make it calm and motionless.

clue.text: Commercial traveller has to move around, despite censure

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
to rove is to wander about

explanation.surface: A salesman keeps travelling despite being told off.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuke someone is to express disapproval of them.

clue.text: The man too disorganised to get away

indicators.note: disorganised says the letters of the words before it are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A man is too muddled to manage an escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorganised' rearranges THE MAN TOO; 'to get' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent from their house is out, gone elsewhere.

clue.text: Award given by former Amer president

definitions.meaning: a sum of money given, for study or a project
Ulysses S. ..., US president 1869-77 and Civil War general

explanation.surface: A prize was presented by an ex-president of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A funding allocation is a type of award, and Ulysses Grant was the eighteenth American president.

clue.text: Understanding part of the student entertainment

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Getting on well is just part of student life.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly agreement between parties, a mutual understanding.

clue.text: Amin transported by British Airways around one African state

indicators.note: transported means the letters of the name are carried into a new order
around says the airline's initials enclose the letter for one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Idi Amin is flown by British Airways to an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: Idi Amin was the Ugandan dictator of the 1970s; 'by' only places his rearranged name beside the airline, which goes 'around' the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a country in south-west Africa.

clue.text: London area where Helvetians feel at home

definitions.text: London area where Helvetians feel at home

parts.words: London area where Helvetians feel at home
parts.note: Helvetians are the Swiss; the district of north-west London whose name sounds like a Swiss chalet would make them feel at home

explanation.surface: Swiss visitors find a corner of London homely.
explanation.walkthrough: Helvetia is the Latin name for Switzerland; the district is in north-west London near Hampstead.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a residential district of north-west London named after a chalet-style inn.

clue.text: Just the racer to beat the favourite

parts.note: to whip is to beat
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A punter seeks a runner able to beat the favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippet is a slim dog bred for racing.

clue.text: Endeavour to find a substitute typist in sober environment

indicators.note: environment means the abbreviation for sober surrounds the typist

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so sober
a temp is a temporary office worker standing in for another

explanation.surface: An office tries to find a stand-in secretary who doesn't drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A try or effort at doing something is an endeavour.

clue.text: Had the tenner changed on the spot

indicators.note: changed says the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone broke a ten-pound note immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changed' fits the money surface, as with a banknote broken into coins, but it rearranges HAD THE TENNER.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means immediately, at that very time and place.

clue.text: What successful street-traders do

parts.note: traders who do well get rid of their entire stock

explanation.surface: Market stallholders have a good day.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling all of one's stock is the aim of any stallholder.

clue.text: Only one of the team is incompetent, it could be argued

definitions.text: Only one of the team is incompetent, it could be argued

parts.words: Only one of the team is incompetent, it could be argued
parts.note: if one player of an eleven-man side is useless, ten are capable; and a position that can be argued is defensible

explanation.surface: A pundit claims just one player in the side is hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket or football team has eleven players, so with one incompetent, ten are able.
explanation.definitionFit: A position that can be maintained in argument is defensible.

clue.text: Inner circle puts former copper in charge

indicators.note: in says the coin's letter is placed inside the word for charge

parts.note: care means charge, as in in someone's care
d was the symbol for the old British penny, a copper coin before 1971

explanation.surface: A clique installs an ex-policeman as boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman; it is the old penny, d, Britain's pre-decimal copper coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a small core group of trained activists.

clue.text: Generally how the batsman is finally assessed

definitions.text: how the batsman is finally assessed
definitions.meaning: a cricket batsman's season is judged by runs per innings

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman is usually judged by the final numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman's average is total runs divided by dismissals, the standard measure of performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Typically means usually, and a cricketer's batting is measured by mean runs per dismissal.

clue.text: Arthur and I have difficulty swallowing a vegetable

parts.note: Art is a short form of the name Arthur
to choke is to struggle to swallow

explanation.surface: Two diners struggle to get a vegetable down.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe kind is a thistle-like plant eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Will examine the composition of Manet

parts.note: to test is to examine

indicators.note: the composition of means the painter's name is rearranged into new letters

explanation.surface: Inspecting the make-up of a Manet painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Manet was the French painter, so 'composition' looks like art criticism; it rearranges MANET to AMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal document disposing of property after death is a will.

clue.text: Hardly the protest upstanding citizens support

definitions.text: Hardly the protest upstanding citizens support

parts.words: Hardly the protest upstanding citizens support
parts.note: upstanding read literally means on their feet, so they would not join a protest where people stay seated

explanation.surface: Respectable people would not back such a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' means respectable but is read literally as standing up.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a protest in which demonstrators occupy a place by sitting.

clue.text: Attribute necessary for a recorder

parts.note: a scribe writes down records

explanation.surface: A quality required by anyone making records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorder' suggests the musical instrument; it is a person who writes things down.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit something to a cause or person is to attribute it.

clue.text: Country lad in a small hay cart

parts.note: a wain is a farm wagon

explanation.surface: A rustic youth rides in a little hay wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is a young rural man, often a lover.

clue.text: Get public transport over, love It's freezing

indicators.note: over means the word for public transport is turned back to front

parts.note: a bus is public transport
love in tennis means a score of nothing

explanation.surface: Catching a bus to see your loved one on a cold day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is the tennis score of nil, so nothing; the clue is printed without its comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperatures below nought degrees are freezing.

clue.text: Contract to construct a viaduct

parts.note: a viaduct is a long bridge

explanation.surface: Signing a deal for the building of a viaduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' reads as a business agreement; it is the verb, to shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text is to cut it down.

clue.text: The thing

definitions.meaning: the word the is the definite ... in grammar

explanation.definitionFit: Grammar calls the word for 'the' the definite one, and an item or object is also so called.

clue.text: It happens to be a level junction

parts.note: even means level
a T-junction, where one road meets another at right angles

explanation.surface: An accident happens at a flat crossroads.
explanation.definitionFit: An occurrence is something that happens.

clue.text: Show Tom with his middle un clad

indicators.note: with his middle says the naked word fills the centre of the tomcat

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
unclad means naked, bare

explanation.surface: A man called Tom displays himself with his midriff exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name; it is a tomcat. 'Un clad' is unclad split in printing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub entertainment, a show.

clue.text: Back injury I have found wear, ing

indicators.note: back means the word for injury is read in reverse order

parts.note: a sore is an injury
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone finds their back injury is wearing them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like the injured part; it turns SORE to EROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that wears away gradually, as water on rock, is corrosive in this sense.

clue.text: The cricket match must be starting late

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket
a match that must be starting is due to begin

explanation.surface: A cricket match is on the point of starting.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind schedule or past the expected time means tardy.

clue.text: Where Yorkists and Lancastrians fought in secret

definitions.meaning: the Wars of the Roses, between the houses of York and Lancaster, were fought under their rose emblems

explanation.surface: England's medieval civil war was conducted covertly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wars of the Roses (1455-87) set the white rose of York against the red of Lancaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin sub rosa means confidentially, and the warring houses fought with the rose as their badge.
